'''''Acis trichophylla''''', [[common name|commonly]] called the '''triangular-leaved snowflake''',<ref>[[Elizabeth Lawrence (writer)|Elizabeth Lawrence]]. ''The Little Bulbs: A Tale of Two Gardens.'' Duke University Press, 1986. [1st pub. Criterion, 1954] [https://books.google.com/books?id=iD_ari9u_IEC&pg=PA36 p. 36.] {{ISBN|9780822307396}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Amaryllidaceae]], native to Portugal, Spain and Morocco.<ref name=WCSP_309235/> It has very narrow leaves. The flowers are produced in late winter or early spring and are usually white, but sometimes pink-tinged or all pink. The species is cultivated as an [[ornamental bulb]], but requires protection from hard frost.

==Description==
''Acis trichophylla'' is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]], growing up to {{Convert|30|cm|abbr=on}} tall, although usually shorter. There are generally three very narrow leaves per bulb, appearing before the flowers, each leaf being up to {{Convert|18|cm|abbr=on}} long but only at most 1 mm wide. Flowering is in late winter or early spring. The flowers are white, sometimes with pink tinges or occasionally all pink, and are arranged in groups of two to four on a stem ([[Scape (botany)|scape]]) that is about as long as or longer than the leaves. Each flower is borne on a long stalk ([[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]), up to 45 or 60 mm long, and has six [[tepal]]s, 12–20 mm long, with sharp tips, that open widely to form a bell shape. The two [[spathe]]s are shorter than the pedicels. The [[Style (botany)|style]] is slightly longer than the [[stamen]]s.<ref name=GreyMathBlam81/><ref name=Math87/><ref name=FE/><ref name=FI/>

==Taxonomy==
The nomenclature of ''Acis trichophylla'' is somewhat complex. The epithet ''trichophyllum'' was first published, in the combination ''Leucojum trichophyllum'', by [[Peter Schousboe]] in 1800.<ref name=IPNI_65764-1/><ref name=Scho00/> The combination was used again as a supposedly new name by [[Félix Avelar Brotero|Félix Brotero]] in 1804,<ref name=Brot04/> but as it had already been published in 1800, ''Leucojum trichophyllum'' <small>Brot.</small> is an illegitimate later [[homonym (biology)|homonym]].<ref name=WCSP_309235/> In 1829, [[Robert Sweet (botanist)|Robert Sweet]] suggested that ''Leucojum trichophyllum'' belonged in ''Acis'', but did not explicitly use the combination ''Acis trichophylla'' nor make clear whose ''Leucojum'' name he meant.<ref name=Swee29/> The combination ''Acis trichophylla'' was first used in 1830 by [[George Don]], referring to Sweet (he actually used the masculine form ''trichophyllus'').<ref name=Don30/>

Although [[William Herbert (botanist)|William Herbert]] in 1837 also placed the species in ''Acis'',<ref name=Herb37/> most later botanists used the genus ''[[Leucojum]]'', treating it as ''L. trichophyllum'' <small>Schousb.</small><ref name=GreyMathBlam81/><ref name=Math87/><ref name=FE/> In 2004, it was restored to ''Acis'', along with other species of ''Leucojum'', on the basis of a [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic]] study.<ref name=Lled04/>

A number of infraspecies have been described, none of which are recognized by the [[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] {{As of|2017|December|lc=yes}}.<ref name=WCSP_309235/> Forms with pinkish flowers have been called f. ''broteri'' and f. ''purpurascens'', those with larger flowers var. ''grandiflorum''.<ref name=Math87/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Acis trichophylla'' is found in central and southern [[Portugal]], south central and south-western [[Spain]] and across the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] in [[Morocco]].<ref name=WCSP_309235/> It is found in dry sandy ground.<ref name=GreyMathBlam81/>

==Cultivation==
''Acis trichophylla'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental bulb]]. It requires protection from frost, and warm dry conditions for a long time in summer, hence growing in an [[alpine house]] or [[bulb frame]] is recommended. Unless planted deeply, around {{Convert|15|cm|4=0|abbr=on}}, it tends to divide into small non-flowering bulbs.<ref name=Math87/>
